forbiddenZones.FZ-1: Production secrets accessible to an agent
forbiddenZones.FZ-2: Organization-wide scope for a single-repository task

A+.title: Codokey Aligned
A+.meaning: Every control is self-attested as implemented with evidence available.

A.title: Controlled With Gaps
A.meaning: All critical controls are implemented; at least one high or medium control is not.

B.title: Partially Governed
B.meaning: At least one critical control is not implemented, but no forbidden-zone control has failed and at least half of critical controls are implemented.

C.title: Ungoverned AI Code Access
C.meaning: A forbidden-zone control has failed, or more than half of critical controls are not implemented.

controls.title: AI involvement in a change is recorded in commit or pull-request metadata
controls.evidence: Commit trailers, PR labels, or bot/app author identities that mark AI-generated or AI-assisted changes, observable on a sample of recent merged PRs.
controls.remediation: Adopt one machine-readable convention (for example a commit trailer or a PR label applied by the agent integration) and verify it on merged history.

controls.title: Each agent acts under a distinct, attributable identity — not a shared account or a reused personal credential
controls.evidence: Inventory mapping each agent integration to its own app, bot, or service identity, plus the human principal who delegated the task; sample audit events showing that identity.
controls.remediation: Provision a dedicated identity per agent integration; retire shared tokens and personal access tokens used by automation.

controls.title: SDLC policy states how AI-assisted changes are disclosed and what review obligation they carry
controls.evidence: Current, approved policy text with owner and review date.
controls.remediation: Add an AI-assisted change section to the SDLC policy: disclosure convention, review obligation, and exceptions process.

controls.title: Human-authored and agent-authored contributions are distinguishable in version-control history
controls.evidence: History query that separates agent-authored commits (by identity or trailer) from human commits for a chosen period.
controls.remediation: Combine CK-OR-01 metadata with CK-OR-02 identities so history can be filtered by author type.

controls.title: Secret scanning is enabled on all active repositories
controls.evidence: Platform security settings or API output showing secret scanning enabled per repository; list of exclusions with justification.
controls.remediation: Enable secret scanning organization-wide; track repositories where it is unavailable and compensate with CI scanning.

controls.title: Secrets are blocked before they enter the repository (server-side push protection, with client hooks as a supplement)
controls.evidence: Push-protection setting enabled; a test push of a synthetic secret pattern rejected; documented bypass process.
controls.remediation: Enable server-side push protection. Client-side pre-commit hooks can be skipped by the committer and should not be the only control.

controls.title: Secret-bearing files (.env, credential files, key material) are outside agent read scope, enforced at a technical boundary
controls.evidence: Agent configuration deny rules or sandbox/filesystem policy covering secret paths, plus a test showing a read attempt is refused; note whether subprocesses are covered.
controls.remediation: Keep secrets out of the working tree (inject at runtime from a secret manager). Where files must exist, combine tool-level deny rules with OS or sandbox isolation — tool-level exclusions alone may not cover subprocesses.

controls.title: Hardcoded-credential review of code and history performed within a defined interval (default: 90 days)
controls.evidence: Dated scan report covering full history and the follow-up record for each finding.
controls.remediation: Schedule a full-history scan; revoke and rotate any confirmed credential before removing it from history.

controls.title: Credential rotation policy is documented and enforced (expiry or automated rotation)
controls.evidence: Policy with lifetimes per credential class; system evidence of expiry or rotation (e.g. token expiration dates).
controls.remediation: Set maximum lifetimes per class; prefer short-lived, automatically issued credentials for agents and CI.

controls.title: Production secrets live in a separate store that agent identities cannot read
controls.evidence: Access policy of the production secret store listing principals; confirmation no agent identity is among them.
controls.remediation: Move production secrets to a dedicated store or protected environment and remove agent identities from its access policy.

controls.title: Each agent has a documented scope: repositories, branches, tools, and permitted actions
controls.evidence: Agent access policy entry per agent (see Reference Kit template) with owner and review date.
controls.remediation: Complete an agent access policy entry for every agent integration before it runs again.

controls.title: Agent credentials grant only the repository permissions the task requires
controls.evidence: Granted permission set for each agent identity compared with the documented scope (CK-AA-01); no unexplained write or admin permissions.
controls.remediation: Replace broad tokens with fine-grained or app installation tokens restricted to the needed repositories and permissions.

controls.title: MCP servers and other agent tool connections are inventoried and reviewed
controls.evidence: Inventory listing each server/tool, its credentials, scopes, and an approval record; an empty inventory counts if verified.
controls.remediation: Inventory configured tool servers per agent; remove unapproved ones; record approval and owner.

controls.title: Agent token scopes are reviewed on a schedule (default: quarterly) and use the shortest practical lifetime
controls.evidence: Dated review record; token metadata showing scopes and expiry.
controls.remediation: Add agent tokens to the access-review cycle; set expirations; declare minimum workflow token permissions explicitly.

controls.title: Organization-wide agent access is disabled by default; repository access is granted per repository
controls.evidence: Agent app/token configuration showing selected-repository access rather than all repositories.
controls.remediation: Switch installations and tokens from "all repositories" to an explicit repository list.

controls.title: Forbidden access zones are defined in writing and enforced technically
controls.evidence: Written forbidden-zone list and, for each zone, the technical control that enforces it (deny rule, permission, protection rule).
controls.remediation: Map each forbidden zone to an enforcing control; a zone enforced only by policy text remains open.

controls.title: Merges of agent-generated changes require approval by a human other than the agent and the person who requested the change
controls.evidence: Branch protection or ruleset export: required approvals ≥ 1, approval of the most recent push required, requester/self-approval not counted.
controls.remediation: Require pull-request approval on protected branches and enable "approval of the most recent reviewable push"; confirm the requester cannot approve.

controls.title: Changes to secret-handling code, CI configuration, or deployment paths require review by a designated owner
controls.evidence: Ownership file (e.g. CODEOWNERS) covering those paths and a protection rule requiring owner review.
controls.remediation: Assign owners to sensitive paths and require code-owner review on protected branches.

controls.title: Reviewers are briefed on failure modes typical of AI-generated changes
controls.evidence: Training or guidance material and attendance/acknowledgement record.
controls.remediation: Adopt the AI-generated PR review checklist in the Reference Kit and brief reviewers on it.

controls.title: Review bypass is technically prevented — including for administrators — not just prohibited by policy
controls.evidence: Protection setting that applies rules to administrators/bypass roles; list of any bypass actors with justification.
controls.remediation: Enable the setting that applies protection to administrators and remove standing bypass permissions.

controls.title: Human review gates are documented in the SDLC governance policy
controls.evidence: Policy section describing each gate and its enforcing control.
controls.remediation: Document each gate alongside the control that enforces it.

controls.title: No agent can deploy to production without an approving human gate
controls.evidence: Production environment protection: required reviewers, self-review prevented; no agent identity among allowed deployers or approvers.
controls.remediation: Protect the production environment with required human approvers and prevent the triggering identity from approving.

controls.title: Production credentials are separated from development and agent environments
controls.evidence: Environment-scoped secrets released only to production deployment jobs after approval; development and agent sessions hold none.
controls.remediation: Scope production secrets to the protected environment so they are released only after its rules pass.

controls.title: CI/CD pipeline includes secret scanning as a blocking step
controls.evidence: Pipeline definition with a secret-scanning job marked required; a failing run blocking merge or deploy.
controls.remediation: Add a required secret-scanning job to the pipeline.

controls.title: Deployment rollback procedures are documented and tested
controls.evidence: Runbook and the date and outcome of the last rollback test.
controls.remediation: Write and exercise a rollback runbook for each production service.

controls.title: Infrastructure-as-code and pipeline-definition changes require review separate from application code
controls.evidence: Ownership rules on IaC and workflow paths routing them to infrastructure/security owners.
controls.remediation: Route IaC and workflow files to dedicated owners via code-owner rules.

controls.title: Agent actions are logged with agent identity, delegating human, timestamp, target, and outcome
controls.evidence: Sample audit records for an agent session containing each field (see Audit Evidence Specification).
controls.remediation: Enable platform audit logging and agent session logs; correlate them by session identifier.

controls.title: Audit logs are protected from modification or deletion by agents and the identities they use
controls.evidence: Log destination access policy showing agent identities lack write/delete; retention lock or append-only configuration.
controls.remediation: Stream logs to a store outside agent reach with write-once or retention-lock settings.

controls.title: Log retention meets your documented requirement, including export beyond platform defaults
controls.evidence: Documented retention requirement and the configured retention of every log source used for reconstruction.
controls.remediation: Compare platform retention windows with your requirement; export logs where the platform window is shorter.

controls.title: Secret exposure events trigger a documented response: revoke, rotate, scope the exposure, record
controls.evidence: Incident runbook for secret exposure and a record of its last exercise or use.
controls.remediation: Write a secret-exposure runbook that starts with revocation and rotation, then determines which sessions had the secret in scope.

controls.title: Audit reviews are scheduled — not only performed after incidents
controls.evidence: Review calendar and the most recent review record.
controls.remediation: Schedule periodic review of agent activity logs.

controls.title: Open governance gaps are tracked with owners and reviewed by engineering leadership (default: quarterly)
controls.evidence: Gap register (for example an exported scorecard result) with owners, dates, and review minutes.
controls.remediation: Export this assessment, assign an owner per unresolved control, and review progress on a fixed cadence.
